outcome: The sexy prime conjecture (infinitely many prime pairs differing by 6) remains completely open; no source claims a proof, disproof, or any result that narrows this specific case, despite a burst of activity in the adjacent bounded-gaps-between-primes problem during August-September 2026.
summary: The sexy prime conjecture asks whether there are infinitely many prime pairs (p, p+6). As of the frozen revision, the only known route to it was the Polymath group's 2014 result that the generalized Elliott-Halberstam conjecture (GEH) implies infinitely many consecutive prime pairs differing by at most 6 (i.e. twin, cousin, or sexy primes) -- but GEH itself remains unproven, and no unconditional route reaches a gap as small as 6. I confirmed via the current Sexy primes and Polignac's conjecture Wikipedia articles that this is still exactly the state of the art: no proof, disproof, or narrowing of this specific case has occurred since 26 January 2024. Separately, I checked a recent flurry of activity on the *general* bounded-gaps-between-primes problem (the 'H1' constant, i.e. liminf of gaps between consecutive primes), since this is the natural place a case-6 result would show up. In this window: Polymath8b's H1<=246 (2014) stood until an OpenAI-credited result (dated around 30 August 2026, cdn.openai.com/pdf/.../short_gaps.pdf and the openai/PrimeGaps186 GitHub repo) claimed H1<=186 via a Lean formalization that is explicitly conditional on three unproven input axioms and contains three acknowledged theorem placeholders -- i.e. an unverified, incomplete, conditional claim, not a checked proof. Days later, Julia Stadlmann (human mathematician) posted an unconditional H1<=240 (arXiv 2608.31126, ~31 August 2026), and a further unconditional H1<=212 followed around 3 September 2026. None of these -- OpenAI's conditional 186, Stadlmann's 240, or the 212 result -- come remotely close to gap=6, and per the task's own scope rule an 'are there infinitely many X' question is not advanced by narrowing a bound unless the bound itself is the question asked; here the question is specifically about gap 6, and the general H1 constant is a different (much weaker, much larger) quantity. I therefore classify this as no_change_found: true. The OpenAI H1<=186 episode is itself an interesting AI-adjacent incident (an AI-attributed, Lean-formalized but axiom-conditional and admittedly incomplete claim, quickly overtaken by an unconditional human proof of a weaker bound) but it is not a result on this problem and I have not recorded it as an event here, since the sexy-prime bullet itself saw no movement at all.
competing_reading: One could argue that any tightening of the general bounded-gaps record is 'progress toward' sexy primes in a loose colloquial sense, since sexy primes are the case gap=6 of the same underlying liminf quantity. But per the task's rule, a case is only advanced when the specific case itself is settled or the general result's scope actually reaches it; H1<=186 (or 212, or 240) says nothing about whether gap-6 pairs are infinite, only that *some* gap <=186 recurs infinitely often. This is a related/general problem, not a narrowing of the sexy-prime case, so I did not code it as partial or progress.
what_would_settle_it: A proof (conditional or unconditional) that liminf of prime gaps is <=6, or a direct resolution of the sexy prime conjecture itself, or a proof of the generalized Elliott-Halberstam conjecture (which the 2014 Polymath result shows would suffice), or a disproof/counterexample showing only finitely many sexy prime pairs exist.

dead_ends: OpenAI's H1<=186 Lean formalization looked initially like it could be a major AI-generated proof event, but it is explicitly conditional on three unproven axioms with acknowledged placeholder theorems, and in any case addresses a general constant (186) nowhere near gap=6, so it does not bear on this problem
